novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement hypothesis—not merely a new setting—in the phrase “a detect-then-reroute circuit” where an “inconsistency detector” suppresses the current path and elevates alternatives, with emergence through RL. The closest prior works found include SCoRe (2024), which trains self-correction behavior behaviorally, Gandhi et al. (2024) on search/backtracking behavior, and “From Reasoning to Answer: Empirical, Attention-Based and Mechanistic Insights into Distilled DeepSeek R1 Models” (2025), which identifies reasoning-focus heads and causal dependence on reasoning tokens but not an error-detection-to-rerouting circuit; search angles included “LLM mechanistic interpretability backtracking circuit,” “self-correction error detector activation patching,” “RL-trained reasoning aha moment mechanism,” and “reasoning-focus heads self-reflection.” The step from these works to the claim requires a new core relationship—localized inconsistency detection causally driving suppression and alternative-token selection—although activation patching and head analysis themselves are standard, so this is a substantive within-field innovation rather than a paradigm-level method.
